name: Kingdom of Chiang Mai
native: อาณาจักรเชียงใหม่

predecessors.name: Lan Na
predecessors.text: Lan Na, the Chiang Mai kingdom under Burmese governors

predecessors.name: Konbaung dynasty
predecessors.text: Burmese-held Chiang Mai and the Lan Na cities

successors.name: Rattanakosin Kingdom (Siam)
successors.text: the Chiang Mai kingdom, annexed as Monthon Phayap

ledger.x: 15 January 1775: the Siamese take Chiang Mai from the Burmese.
January 1775: Lan Na passes from Burma to Chiang Mai and Thonburi.
1777: Chiang Mai is abandoned and the realm is held from Kawila's Lampang.
March 1788: the Burmese are beaten at Lampang and Pasang.
March 1797: Kawila re-enters Chiang Mai and the seat returns.
December 1802: Kawila becomes tributary king of Chiang Mai.
1804: Chiang Saen is taken from the Burmese.
July 1853: Mahawong is appointed King Mahotaraprathet of Chiang Mai after King Mongkut raised the Lanna lords from Phraya to Chao in 1853.
1892: the Trans-Salween towns go to British Burma.
December 1899: Chiang Mai is annexed as Monthon Phayap.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Chiang Mai (1774-1775)
wars.outcome: Chiang Mai taken on 15 January 1775; Lan Na became a Thonburi tributary; the Burmese counterattack from Chiang Saen of September 1775 failed.

wars.name: Burmese sieges of Lampang (Nine Armies' War)
wars.outcome: Kawila held Lampang against 30,000 Burmese in 1785-1786 and 45,000 in 1788; the Burmese were beaten at Lampang and Pasang in March 1788.

wars.name: Burmese invasions of Chiang Mai (1797-1798, 1802)
wars.outcome: Repelled in April 1798 and again in 1802 by Siamese relief forces; Bodawpaya had set up Chom Hong at Mong Hsat in 1802 as a rival.

wars.name: Capture of Chiang Saen
wars.outcome: Chiang Saen taken in 1804 by combined forces from Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Lampang, Nan and Vientiane; Anouvong of Vientiane took part.

wars.name: Chiang Mai campaigns against Kengtung
wars.outcome: Kengtung captured in 1802 and Mong Yawng in 1805; Lanna forces beaten in 1808; Maha Hkanan accepted Burmese suzerainty in 1813; the attacks of 1850 and March 1853 failed.

certainty.note: No treaty line: the frontiers with Burma (Salween, Kengtung), Nan, Phrae and Luang Prabang are approximate.
